b1-PI-A: This protocol is meant to be done in phases. Don't skip any, since you only move on to the next phase if the one you're on doesn't clear up your symptoms.
b1-P1-A:
Phase 1: The Pre-Flight Safety Check (The Mechanic & Electrician)
This first phase comes from T.C. Hale (Kick Your Fat in the Nuts) and Stanley Rosenberg (Accessing the Healing Power of the Vagus Nerve). Before you add "fuel" (supplements) or "fire" (antimicrobials), you have to make sure the engine is mechanically sound.
Hale starts with your autonomic tone. Are your pupils dilated all the time? Is your gag reflex absent? If yes, you're in "Sympathetic Dominance" (fight/flight), and your digestion is offline.
To fix that, Rosenberg has you do the "Basic Exercise" (eye movements) or "The Salamander" to mechanically release the Vagus nerve and switch your body into "Rest and Digest."
Next is bile flow, and that's Hale again. Do you burp after fatty meals? Do your stools float or look clay-colored? If yes, your bile is stagnant, and adding the "fire" now (antimicrobials) will cause a "herx" reaction you can't detoxify.
Hale's fix is to thin the bile with Beet Flow or Phosphatidylcholine before you start any killing protocol.
My notes: for stress and sleep see Severe stress above, and for stomach acid and bile see Low stomach acid.
b1-P2-A:
Phase 2: The Reset (The Architect & Scientist)
For the reset you follow Dr. Michael Ruscio (Healthy Gut, Healthy You) and Dr. Mark Pimentel (The Microbiome Connection). The point is to reduce inflammation and starve the overgrowths, without harsh chemicals.
Start with the diet. Adopt a Paleo-Low FODMAP diet (Ruscio) or a Low Fermentation Eating plan (Pimentel), since either way the goal is to stop feeding the bacteria in your small intestine.
Pimentel also wants your meals strictly spaced 4-5 hours apart, with no snacking. Why so strict? Because it allows the Migrating Motor Complex (MMC) to sweep your gut clean.
My notes: see Poor diet now and Plant foods, above.
b1-P3-A:
Phase 3: The Purge (The Restorer)
If the diet didn't clear your symptoms, an active overgrowth (SIBO/SIFO) is likely present. Here you're following Dr. William Davis (Super Gut), and Dr. Michael Ruscio again.
Davis recommends using specific herbal combinations like Candibactin AR/BR or FC Cidal/Dysbiocide for 4 weeks. But AVOID most herbal antibiotics.
H2O2 actually works better than the herbal antibiotics according to me and orthomolecular drs. My BFF Pooyan tried candibactin actually and it nearly killed him. The H2O2 worked a lot better without side effects. There is one herbal antibiotic that works really well tho for H. pylori: Berberine. If you have an acute infection with something that those don't help quickly, consider escalating to secnidazole treatment for rapid cure, and paromomycin post-treatment for relapse prevention, with medical supervision.
BIND to the toxins, especially the metals and parasite die-off toxins, using Zholy3O.
While you're in the kill phase, take Ruscio's triple probiotic alongside it: a blend of Lacto/Bifido, S. boulardii, and soil-based organisms. It's there to maintain diversity and prevent opportunistic infections (like C. diff).
If the herbs failed, that means the overgrowth is too severe, or your gut lining is too damaged for solids. Ruscio's "Nuclear" Option for that is the Elemental Diet, a 2-3 week liquid-only diet (predigested nutrients). It starves the bacteria completely while nourishing you, the human host.
My notes: the H2O2 swap above is mine, not the books'. For berberine and H. pylori see Parasites, and for SIBO yogurt see SIBO, above.
b1-P4-A:
Phase 4: The Investigation (The Detective)
This phase is all Benjamin Brown (Digestive Health Solution), for when even the "Nuclear Option" failed. At that point the microbiome is ruled out, and the problem is likely organ failure, environmental toxicity, or brain plasticity. (The last two are Phase 6, below.)
So here, you check the organs. Is it your pancreas? Test for Exocrine Pancreatic Insufficiency (Stool Elastase). Or is it Bile Acid Diarrhea? That's the SeHCAT test. Then treat with high-dose enzymes or bile binders, depending on what you find.

b1-P5-A:
Phase 5: Restoration & Maintenance (The Gardener)
Once you're clear of infection, you have to rebuild a diverse ecosystem to prevent relapse. Dr. William Davis is back for that, along with Dr. Will Bulsiewicz (Fiber Fueled).
Start by re-seeding with Davis's high-dose "SIBO Yogurt", fermented for 36 hours. It contains L. reuteri, to heal the lining and boost oxytocin, and L. gasseri, to produce bacteriocins that kill SIBO.
Then feed the new healthy bacteria. Bulsiewicz says to slowly titrate plant diversity back into your diet, aiming for 30+ different plants per week.
Continue Pimentel's strict meal spacing from Phase 2 (4+ hours this time), forever, to keep the MMC cleaning wave active.
And fuel the mitochondria: see the fuels under Leaky gut, above (glutamine, butyrate and TCA intermediates).
My notes: see Leaky gut above for colostrum, zinc carnosine, BPC-157, ozonated zeolite and the fuels, and Sitting above for movement and yoga.
b1-P6-A:
Phase 6: Refractory Cases (The Hazmat Team)
Are you "sensitive to everything"? Or do you relapse right away, even though you've stuck to the protocol perfectly? That's what this last phase is for, and it comes from Neil Nathan (Toxic) and Annie Hopper (Wired for Healing).
Nathan's first check is your environment. Could it be mold/mycotoxins, or Lyme? Assess for those, and if you test positive, use specific binders (Cholestyramine, Charcoal, Clay).
Then Hopper looks at the brain. If you react to everything (that first question again), the issue is Limbic System Impairment. Use her "Brain Retraining" (DNRS) to stop your brain from firing false "danger" signals to the gut.
My notes: Matt's note on mopping up mycotoxins with fermented colostrum is under Leaky gut, above.
